title: Remove a seatbelt twist through its sliding tongue
instruction: Remove the twist from the seatbelt without detaching either end. Leave the webbing flat through the tongue, then release both hands.
context: A twisted seatbelt can be awkward to straighten because its sliding tongue traps the fold. Form a diagonal fold, work it through the slot and spread the webbing flat.
setup: A 500 x 47 x 1.2 mm polyester seatbelt section is attached to two 70 x 22 x 40 mm bench anchors, 440 mm apart. A steel sliding tongue has a 49 x 3.5 mm slot and 1.5 mm thickness. It starts at the midpoint with opposing half-twists trapped on either side. Blue and yellow edge markers show the webbing orientation. Both hands start open. The deterministic settled reset, dimensions and fixed layout are in model.py.
scoring: 1.0: webbing intact, tongue retained on it, crosswise roll below 15 degrees and visible width above 40 mm throughout, and both hands released for 3 seconds. 0.75 for this flat result before release/hold. 0.5 if maximum remaining roll is below 90 degrees but it is not yet flat. Otherwise 0; damage or detached hardware overrides credit. Inspect both edge markers using overhead/side photographs, a ruler and a protractor.
fidelity: Native YAM arms/cameras. Webbing is a flexible mass-point ribbon with stretch, bending, table and coarse self-contact. Continuous edge/slot constraints preserve threading. The tongue is a reduced sliding body; ideal grasps move it. Initial stiction releases after 2 mm of sliding. Detailed weave, calibrated friction and arm reaction forces are omitted. No timed or score-triggered untwisting.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0. Dream completed with 25 server sessions after expiry recoveries.
